 Why SSI Payments for November Are Coming Out Early
 Supplemental Security Income recipients will get November benefits before the month begins. Here's when checks arrive and when the 2027 increase takes effect.
 Supplemental Security Income recipients will get their monthly payment for November during the month of October this year.
 SSI is a program that provides payments to older adults and people who have disabilities and limited income or financial resources. The separate Social Security program provides monthly retirement, disability and survivor benefits, generally based on a worker’s earnings history.
 Both programs are overseen by the Social Security Administration and operate on different payment distribution schedules. Here’s what beneficiaries should know about when to expect their next check.
 Why is SSI being paid on Oct. 30? 
 SSI beneficiaries will get their November payments in October this year.
 That’s because Nov. 1 falls on a Sunday, so the SSA is sending checks out on the preceding business day, Friday, Oct. 30.

 When will I receive my Social Security payments for November? 
 According to the SSA, the schedule for distribution of Social Security checks for November is:
 Tuesday, Nov. 10, for beneficiaries whose birth dates fall between the first and 10th of the month.
 Wednesday, Nov. 18, for beneficiaries whose birth dates fall between the 11th and 20th of the month.
 Wednesday, Nov. 25, for beneficiaries whose birth dates fall between the 21st and 31st of the month.
 When does the annual cost-of-living increase take effect? 
 The 2027 cost-of-living adjustment takes effect in January, with Social Security recipients seeing the 3.6% increase in their January checks.
 SSI recipients will receive their first increased payment a day early, on Dec. 31 because of the New Year’s Day holiday.
